utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. IT-95-14/2-T. The Prosecutor versus Dario Kordic and Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you'd like to sit down, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Colonel Schipper, you are a Lieutenant-Colonel in the Royal Netherlands Army, you graduated from officer school at the Royal Netherlands Military Academy in Breda in 1969; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And in preparing to testify before this Court today, have you reviewed what was put before you as approximately a 9- or 10-page outline of what your testimony would be, or proposed to be?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court, generally speaking, or not generally speaking, can you tell the Court whether that statement is an accurate statement of your recollection of events in Bosnia during the time that you were there in 1993?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: It's an accurate statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I understand, sir, that you were stationed in Central Bosnia from the 20th of April, 1993 to approximately the 3rd of November, 1993 as commanding officer of the Netherlands Belgian U.N. Transport Battalion. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you replaced a Lieutenant-Colonel de Boer in that instance?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You took some steps, Colonel, to inform yourself or be briefed about the political-military situation in Bosnia prior to arriving to take your duties there?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is it correct that you arrived in the former Yugoslavia at Split on the 20th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Actually, it was the 19th. We went up to Busovaca on the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And then you were driven by Colonel de Boer from Split to Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir that on this same drive with Colonel de Boer, you passed the village of Ahmici, which at that time had been substantially destroyed. If you were arriving there on approximately the 20th of April, the events there had happened some days previous. Did Colonel de Boer give you some information that what had happened in Ahmici was the result of ethnic cleansing committed by the HVO a few days earlier?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you notice, as you went through Ahmici, or went by Ahmici, that many of the houses had been burned, some were in fact still burning, the minaret at the mosque had been toppled or blown over?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that you noticed that some houses were untouched, and you later learned that the untouched houses were Croat houses?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct, Colonel, that you had more frequent contact with the HVO side than the army of the BiH because primarily your dealings were in the Busovaca-Vitez pocket which was controlled by the Bosnian Croats?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: However, having said that, it's correct, is it not, that you did have contact with both sides?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you arrived in the Busovaca area, is it fair to say that you observed that many or most of the Muslim families were without their men, if you will, and you learned that many had left for Zenica out of fear?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, Colonel, DutchBat was actually a combined Dutch/Belgian unit, as we mentioned earlier, primarily involved in transportation duties; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: It was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And such as bringing UNPROFOR supplies into Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: UNHCR supplies. It was a UNPROFOR battalion, but UNHCR was the organisation which we were looking for.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You were providing, essentially, escort duties and helping them to get into Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Is it correct, sir, that one of the routes that you used to bring supplies from the Croatian coast was called Route Triangle?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And I think there may have been another one that may have been on part of the route the same, but on other parts of the route different, that was called Route Diamond?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If the usher could show you momentarily and put on the ELMO what has been marked -- actually, there is three separate maps. Unfortunately, we can't seem to get all the information on the same map. But it's 2612,13, 2612,9 and 26 -- sorry -- 12,7. I'm told that the larger ,13 is attached to the back of one of the other packets. I think we can put these on the ELMO and move through them relatively quickly, Your Honour, without shuffling too much paper. I am going to look at these first, Colonel, in the order of 2612,13. Look at approximately the middle of that map. Can you point out the city or village of Metkovic?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: [indicates] It's through here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Was Metkovic one of the routes at one end, if you will, or close to one end of the routes used to bring supplies into Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And was it one of the points or the beginning point of either Route Diamond or Route Triangle?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: One or the other?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, looking on that same map, a little -- approximately in the 11.00 direction, somewhat above and to the left, is there another village or city called Makarska. I'm sorry. Makarska, yes.

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: [Indicating]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell, was that at times related to the shipment of supplies into Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Not at that moment. It was Metkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: On the next map, 261 -- excuse me, 2612.9. Actually, the reason for pointing out Makarska was primarily because the second map was not continuous all the way down to Metkovic, but on this map then we can see the relationship between Makarska and Split. Do you see that? Is it fair to say that, in fact, Split, on the Croatian coast, was again another point at which supplies were brought into Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: It was less important but it was a point, less important.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Less important than Metkovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Then just to complete the orientation, if we go to the map, the last map in that packet, which is 2612.7, a larger scale or a map covering a larger area. We can then see Split in the lower left corner, and on one route -- and then also down at the bottom of the map, more toward the right of the page, we can see the city of Mostar. Can you point that out for the Court, please?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: [Indicating]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, can you just basically show, in your responsibilities as commander of the DutchBat Transportation Battalion, the basic routes that were used -- I think there may have been two -- to transport various supplies into the Central Bosnia area?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: One from Split up to Sinj, Tomislavgrad, then across the mountains to Prozor, Gornji Vakuf, Novi Travnik, Vitez, Busovaca [indicating]. The other route came from Metkovic [indicating].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Which is a problem with this particular map. We can't go all the way to Metkovic. But can you describe the approximate route from Metkovic to Mostar?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: We did not use that route to Mostar, just once.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. What was the more normal route then?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: The normal route was about this way [indicating], and that formed the other route again.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Once you got around the Tomislavgrad area, the route essentially --

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: They were together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very good.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I didn't want to mark the Registry's copies of these maps but we may do, with the Court's permission, submit a further copy which we'll have the witness mark the route if that's agreeable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Moving forward, sir, is it correct that in your experience, during your time in Central Bosnia, Dusko Grubesic was the commander of the Busovaca HVO Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it fair to say, sir, that you met with Mr. Grubesic approximately once or so every two weeks?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that he was one of your principal points of contact on the HVO side?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: During your time in Bosnia did you come to know that the main political leader in Central Bosnia was Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Is that in dispute?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: He was one of the leading political figures in Central Bosnia, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Scott, these are sensitive issues which you really shouldn't lead on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well. We had not discussed with counsel, Your Honour, and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court, Colonel, in your own words, who did you learn to be the principal, if there was one, the principal or main political leader or figure in Central Bosnia during your time there?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: I often heard the name of Mr. Dario Kordic, and I asked my interpreters what was going on and what his position was, and so I learned that he was a very important political leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: During your time there, did you ever come to any understanding whether Mr. Kordic had any military role or military title that he used?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: He used the military title "Colonel."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you know approximately where Mr. Kordic and his family lived in Central Bosnia? I don't mean the street number or anything like that but approximately where he lived.

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: I know it approximately. It was from Busovaca in the direction of Kupres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you have information as to where, if you will, Mr. Kordic spent much of his, if we can use the term, "working day"?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: He was quite often in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you know where in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: At the headquarters of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Was that the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command headquarters?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: I was told it was. I never visited it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you come to know that that was the same headquarters building used by then Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Based on any assessment that the UNPROFOR made and based on your own experience in Bosnia for the months that you were there, how would you rate the level or degree of Mr. Kordic's influence in the area?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Very high.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think this embarks on matters of political opinion that are beyond the stated background of the Colonel, which is obviously an impressive military background. We've made these objections before. I'd just like to register the same objection again with respect to political opinions on the part of Colonel Schipper at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It was not a political question. It was merely a question of influence. It seems to me the witness, having been in the area, is entitled to answer it in the way that he did. We shall, of course, hear further evidence which no doubt will show on what view that was based.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Colonel, your answer was that in your assessment the -- Mr. Kordic's influence was, quote -- I'm simply referring to the transcript, to move on -- "very high." In the course of your time in Bosnia and some of these events we will get to in the course of the morning's testimony, but did you have occasions sometimes to meet directly with Mr. Kordic?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: I met him at a special occasion with the commander of BritBat, some representatives of Red Cross, mayor the Busovaca, myself, Colonel Blaskic, and Mr. Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you happen to meet with him at another dinner party function, if you will, in approximately August of that --

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: He was also present at a dinner party where we celebrated their 622nd birthday of the town of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that UNPROFOR, on the basis of various intelligence and information gathering, had also made certain assessments and communicated those to the commanding officers in the area?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Are these some of the things on which you base the conclusion that you stated a few minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you advise the Court what was your observation or information as to any relationship, working relationship between Mr. Kordic and Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: When I saw Mr. Kordic, I always saw Mr. Blaskic as well. I got the impression that they were working very close together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you have any assessment on the Bosnian-Croat side, on the HVO side, who were the leaders in that Vitez-Busovaca area who seemed to make most of the decisions or handle the issues that you -- for instance, when things came up with you or with UNPROFOR, who would handle those kind of decisions?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Kordic and Blaskic --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just register a brief objection at this point. I don't think that the witness is competent to issue an opinion of the type he's been asked to. And I don't mean to interrupt Mr. Scott, but it appears from the foundation that's been laid that this opinion is going to be based upon a grand total of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would you slow down, please, Mr. Sayers. Could the Defence counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That goes to the weight of the opinion, the weight of the evidence. It doesn't go to whether the witness is entitled to give it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, this is a constant objection, if I may say, and we have consistently ruled against you. Now, you can take this as a ruling and, unless you've got a different point, kindly don't make the objection again. I can't stop you objecting, but it's not going to be helpful to be constantly interrupted on precisely the same point. The issue in these cases is whether the witness, having met people, had meetings with them, having been in the area, usually the term is six months, I don't think we have it precisely in the case of this witness, is entitled to express an opinion as to who, as it were, was in charge, or who had the greater influence, or who was making the decisions. Now, the rule, of course, is that usually only experts can give opinions, but this is really evidence of fact. He is saying that: It appears to me that 'X' was in charge; 'X' had the greater influence; 'X' made the decisions, something along those lines. Now, as I say, I think this is essentially a matter of fact. How much weight the Tribunal gives to it is, of course, a matter which has to be determined. But it seems to me not an issue of admissibility, but an issue of weight, and of course on that you are entitled to cross-examine. You are entitled to put the matters which you put to us to the witness and say: Well, is your view based on this or on as little as that? And then, of course, that also goes to the weight. So I think, perhaps, that is the most straightforward way to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. President, thank you very much. I agree entirely. And we will not make any further objections upon that basis, since I believe the Court has articulated its views on that particular subject totally and clearly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, that's not to stop you making some other point, and if there are different considerations that apply, then of course we'll hear them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Colonel, perhaps the best way to proceed -- the transcript on the monitor is scrolled beyond your last answer. Perhaps you can just tell us again, based upon your time there and assessment, et cetera, that have been discussed in the last 10 or 15 minutes or so, who did it appear to you to be the leaders or decision-makers on the Bosnian Croat side in the Busovaca-Vitez area?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Kordic and Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How would you assess the relative roles of the two, in terms of on military matters?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Colonel Blaskic was the military expert for Mr. Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Colonel, you have been in the Dutch army since approximately 1969. Is it based on your training, your exposure to military doctrine, your own personal experience, is it fair to say that a military commander is a political or policy tool?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: A decision to engage in combat or warfare is ultimately a political or policy decision?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And in that context, the military then essentially becomes the technical executor of that policy?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In the Central Bosnia area you understood that Colonel Blaskic was the commander of that operational zone; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court, based upon your approximate six-months duty in Central Bosnia, were you aware of any instances where Colonel Blaskic's orders were disobeyed or not followed?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: To your knowledge, sir, was it Colonel Blaskic or, in any event, the HVO headquarters in Vitez where you would go, you or UNPROFOR would go to raise any issues in the area as they related to military matters?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct to say, sir, that based on your military training and experience, is it your judgement that Colonel Blaskic would not have allowed any other components, if you will, of the HVO, of the Bosnian-Croat military or paramilitary forces, to operate in his area without his knowledge and agreement?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No, he wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Why is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Because an area commander, a commander has area responsibility. They will never allow even friendly troops to operate in his area without his knowledge beforehand.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Why is that?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: It's getting pretty critical when troops which you do not know are present, starting to operate without you knowing it or approving it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And again, based on your six months in Bosnia, did there ever come a time, to your knowledge, that there were any troops associated with what we would say the Bosnian-Croat side, be they HVO or described otherwise, to your knowledge any troops or forces on that side that were operational in Central Bosnia without Colonel Blaskic's knowledge?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that at that time in the Vitez pocket you saw some HVO or Bosnian-Croat soldiers dressed in black uniforms, who were working closely with other soldiers who wore camouflage uniforms with HVO patches?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct that on some occasions you saw both of these types of Croat soldiers manning checkpoints together?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Some in black uniforms, some in the camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you hear at times some of the DutchBat officers refer to some of the soldiers in black as HOS or HOS?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: They did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did that seem to you, based on your experience, to note -- distinct any separateness between what may be called the more regular HVO soldiers and the HOS soldiers?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No. Colonel, it might be because I'm also trying to listen to the French translation for the purposes of keeping myself a little slower, but you might also want to speak up just a bit.

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your voice may be a bit soft. To the best of your knowledge and assessment, Colonel Schipper, is it correct that the soldiers that were dressed in black were under Blaskic's command; since again, is it fair to say, you were convinced that Colonel Blaskic would not have allowed forces to operate, at least friendly forces, to operate in his area of responsibility without his knowledge and control?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I want to direct your attention to the 19th of May of 1993. On that day did you accompany BritBat's then commanding officer, an Alastair Duncan, to a meeting at a lodge or a house west of Busovaca in the mountains?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And do you recall who called that meeting?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: The major of Busovaca called it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think you may have said "major." You mean the "mayor"?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Mayor, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Was that Zoran Maric?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: He was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that at this meeting Colonel Blaskic and Mr. Kordic were also present?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Amongst others, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And also was Dusko Grubesic present, to your knowledge, and also Ivan Santic, who was the mayor of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask you what was said at this particular moment, sir, but can you tell the Court whether at this meeting the issue or subject of Ahmici, the attack on Ahmici, came up in conversation?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: It came up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you relate that part of the conversation to the Court, please?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: It started off with the commander of BritBat at that time, who started the discussion with Mr. Kordic and Mr. Blaskic about the things that happened at Ahmici, and then it was said that it was not the responsibility of the HVO in the Vitez area, but there were foreign troops coming in who did the job. I remember Colonel Duncan looking at me with the question mark, "Why is it possible that someone allows foreign troops to be present in the area without knowing it was foreign?" It was a great surprise for us and it was unbelievable.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you can recall, sir, who was doing the speaking in terms of giving the explanation that these were not local HVO forces?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Mr. Kordic was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you use the term "foreign" in this concept, I assume you're not using "foreign" in the terms of foreign country?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No. Not belonging to your own organisation. Could all be friendly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It's fair to say that, based on what you said a moment ago, you and Mr. Duncan, Colonel Duncan, had some doubt about that?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Very much doubt about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: During your tenure in Bosnia, did you ever come to have any information or knowledge that any forces, any person on the Bosnian Croat side, whether described as HVO or HOS or any other force, was punished or disciplined for the events in Ahmici or other Muslim villages in the Vitez pocket?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Never heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In your experience as a military officer and to the extent you're familiar with military doctrine not only in the Netherlands but more on an international basis, can you tell the Court whether a commander's responsibility extends over his area of command, the geographic area of his command responsibilities generally?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: I don't quite understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It wasn't a good question. Forgive me. In this situation, using the explanation that was given to you on the 19th that there were other troops in the area --

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: -- can you tell the Court what responsibility, if any, does a commanding officer have for other friendly forces operating in his area of command?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: The area commander always stays responsible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Why is that?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Because it's his area and he will agree to the coming in other troops, yes or no. If he's overruled, he's no longer the area commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Again, during your time in Bosnia, was there ever any occasions, based on anything that Mr. Blaskic may have said, that Mr. Kordic may have said, that Mr. Grubesic may have said that caused you believe that there were other forces operating on the Bosnian Croat side in Central Bosnia that were not controlled by the HVO --

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No. Colonel Blaskic was still the military area commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Moving forward, going to paragraph 26, Your Honour. Is it correct, Colonel, that during your time in Central Bosnia you knew and had various dealings with the following HVO personnel, if you will: Dusko Grubesic, who you've already said was the commander of the HVO Busovaca Brigade; Pasko Ljubesic; Vlado Cosic; and Anto Sliskovic?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you come to have any impression or observations as to the relationship, if any, between those particular four individuals?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: They were working very close together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct that you met with Pasko Ljubicic and Vlado Cosic on a fairly frequent basis?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: On some of those occasions, sir, can you tell us whether either Mr. Kordic or Colonel Blaskic were also present?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: They were. It was at the anniversary of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In that regard, is it correct, sir, that on approximately the 14th of August, 1993, you and other representatives of UNPROFOR were invited to a dinner with the HVO a couple of days later, actually on the 16th of August, and you were invited by Zoran Maric who was the mayor, if you will, or the president of the Busovaca municipal HVO?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I could direct your attention and have the witness shown, please, Exhibit Z1166,1. Is that a copy, sir, of an invitation that you received to this event, this dinner party on the 16th? Well, the invitation dated the 14th, the dinner dated or proposed for the 16th of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The place of the reception on the invitation is a place called the Vatrostalna Villa at Tisovac?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you and other UNPROFOR officers, in fact, accept this invitation and attend a dinner function, if you will, at the lodge near Tisovac?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can ask the usher to show you and put on the ELMO, please, what's been marked as Exhibit 2780.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I apologise for the glare, Your Honour, on the ELMO. If there are handout copies, the handouts might actually be clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is this a photograph that you took, sir, at this dinner function?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that -- I suspect it won't be disputed -- on our right side of the table, looking at the photograph, in the middle of the photograph is Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And on the opposite side of the table, toward what would be, from our perspective, the left end of the table, the man with his hand to his mouth, that's Colonel Blaskic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who were the UNPROFOR officers who are sitting at the table, do you recall, just in general?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes. The one next to Colonel Blaskic is Lieutenant-Colonel Siliacus, Colonel from Holland, the next one is my driver and opposite is my intelligence officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This dinner was at the Vatrostalna lodge or villa at Tisovac in the mountains somewhere southwest of Busovaca; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can ask the usher to show you what's been marked as Z2781.2. It's a map. I'm sorry. Just briefly, Colonel, could you just point out in the area -- in the general area on that map where you recall this lodge or villa being located? On the ELMO you're probably going to have to --

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: [Indicating]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And just so the record is -- let the record reflect, Your Honour, that the witness is marking -- has pointed to a point about roughly an inch and a half, two inches below the village of Kupres and a little to what would be the -- west of that point, about two inches below it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, was this the same -- by the way, was this the same village or villa where you had gone with Colonel Duncan on, I believe, the 19th of May for the meeting at which the discussion of Ahmici --

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: At this -- looking back to Exhibit 2780, the photograph of the dinner table, is it correct, sir, that also at that same dinner but at a separate table were again Dusko Grubesic, Pasko Ljubicic and Vlado Cosic?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you will go please to -- if the usher can show you two photographs, starting with Z2780.2. Is the man seated on the left, is that Pasko Ljubicic?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And who is the man standing on the right side of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: We know him as Vlado Cosic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if you will go -- and these are two of the people that you had regular dealings with during your tenure in Bosnia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Going to Exhibit Z2780,3. The man holding the rifle there, who is that?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Vlado Cosic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So the same man who was standing to the right in the prior photograph?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court, is that -- the rifle that these three men are examining, is that a 50-calibre sniper rifle?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I would like you to go, before we finish further, go forward with your testimony, I would -- if we could jump ahead for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to ask the witness when was this second photograph taken, the one with the sniper rifle? What was the occasion, and was the witness the one who took the photograph, or who was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour. Very good questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately -- well, first of all, did you take these photographs?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately when and where?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: It was on the Sunday afternoon. We had some sort of regular visit once every week to the local military commanders to discuss problems, to find solutions. And on one of these occasions, the man on the photograph who was bending over, with the dark hair, not holding the rifle, this one [indicates] arrived with this van, and he was pretty excited. Then it appeared that he had a brand new case carrying this gun. I took this photograph to inform my area commander, being Colonel Duncan, that these type of weapons was in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well. Do you recall approximately where you were at this particular occasion?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: At the same place as the photograph shows with Ljubesic and Cosic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Then I'm afraid I must ask the same question about that photograph.

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe we can use the map then.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If that will help. You are looking, for the record, you are looking at Z2781,2.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, okay. And can you point out the approximate area where you recall these photographs being taken?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: I'm not too familiar with those mountains, but it was somewhere in this area [indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So a little bit to the -- well, near the -- what some people would call the Busovaca T-junction?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes. In the mountains.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you give the Court any further assistance on the approximate date or time when the photographs were taken?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: I would say beginning of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I suspect that's probably the best we can do, Your Honour. Thank you. If the usher could next show you Exhibit Z1268,2. Can you tell the Court what that is?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: This is some letter of appreciation given to me by the four persons on the right bottom side of this letter. On the occasion of my return to Holland after my tour of duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And again, the four persons being Pasko Ljubicic, Vlado Cosic, Dusko Grubesic and Anto Sliskovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There's a reference in the second sentence of this short statement to the extent -- making reference to a modest gift.

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did these gentlemen -- did these men give you a gift at that time?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: They did. It was quite surprising. I once came to the Vatrostalna lodge and I saw an animal on a piece of wood. I didn't know the name of the animal, so I asked what sort of animal is that. It was translated by my interpreter to Mr. Dusko Grubesic, and he told me it was a marten. I forgot about the whole incident. And when I left, I invited them at my headquarters, and they gave me this marten as a souvenir before I went back to Holland.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's a pine marten? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Marten. Like a weasel?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yeah, bigger than a weasel. About that size.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Essentially, it was a small stuffed animal?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yeah. It stunk.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, just before we move off this topic, did your relationship with these four men, and perhaps others on the HVO side, change over time? And by that I mean in contrast to your arrival in April, and by the time you left early November of 1993, can you tell the Court whether the nature of your relationship with these individuals changed in any way?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: It changed very much. In the beginning there was an angry feeling about things which had happened in the area. Later on the local brigades had to really defend themselves from attacks from the Muslim factions. So the operations became more military normal. And also our presence in the area was accepted more than it was in the beginning of my tour. So the whole situation, in fact, changed and we became more and more friendly to each other because we all saw the same sort of problems. We wanted to try to operate our convoys and our transports, so we needed freedom of movement. And the local factions tried to defend themselves against other people, and you come to a situation where you really start to understand the problems you both have. And we started to talk more frequent and we exchanged more information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that the individuals on the HVO side became more militarily threatened, if you will, in that area toward the latter part of your tour?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Was it your observation at that time they became friendlier toward UNPROFOR as more perhaps of a supporter, at least a hoped for supporter as opposed to the enemy?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that you got -- over time you would get more and more information from these men. Can you give the Court any specific example as it related to your duties to transport supplies in Bosnia? What kind of information would they give you?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: They did not give the direct information. My convoys consisted of non-protected trucks. So we were eager to have our soldiers on the road as safe as possible. And the information we got was what time and in what direction will you be moving tomorrow. And we told them and they advised us to pass certain points in the area before a certain clock time. And when we did so, we had no trouble of getting into fights or anything else. When we used that information, we had a pretty safe trip down south or up north.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: On any of those occasions did it come to your attention that sometime after you had passed at the appointed time, that fighting then did break out in those areas?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: I got reports from my convoy commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that on one occasion you were asked to take some -- to transport some sick Muslim prisoners who were being held by the HVO in Busovaca to Zenica?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that they were being held in a house, again in the mountains near Busovaca, where they were guarded by HVO soldiers wearing the chequerboard patch?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And the two prisoners were two elderly Muslim male civilians?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In approximately May 1993, do you recall an occasion where approximately 100 Muslim women, children and elderly from the Busovaca area appeared at the Dutch Transport Battalion compound -- and by the way, where was the DutchBat compound located?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: The compound was located in a former hotel in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you recall the name of that former hotel?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: It was a winter sport hotel. I can't recall -- the official name, I can't recall, because we called it Hotel Nunspeet, according to the village I am coming from.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Does the name Hotel Tisa ring any bells?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: It rings a bell.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In any event, it was in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And these 100 Muslim civilians had approached you about being transported to Zenica to join the men and their families; is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you have discussions with Zoran Maric and Dusko Grubesic about the request that you had received to transport these Muslims to Zenica?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: I had, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that Mr. Maric and Mr. Grubesic did not object to your taking these Muslims out of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: They did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you then take steps to, in fact, arrange for the transportation --

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: We started a bus shuttle service.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did it come to your attention, sir, about the following day that Radio Zenica was announcing that either you or perhaps, more generally, DutchBat, was assisting the HVO in ethnic cleansing in the area?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What was your reaction to that?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Stop immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Had it been your intention, sir, to assist the HVO to cleanse Muslims out of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Going to June of 1993. Is it correct that the ABiH attacked and took Travnik; many of the Bosnian Croat inhabitants of Travnik fled to Busovaca, where they started moving into the houses of the remaining Muslim families?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did Mr. Maric again approach you about some sort of assistance in solving the housing problem?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, generally, what did Mr. Maric say to you and what did you say back to him?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: He was complaining about the lack of houses, and I told him that if they had not destroyed Ahmici, the problem maybe never would have arisen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did Mr. Maric say anything to you that he could not guarantee the safety of the Muslim families in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Around that time did you hear through your interpreter that Colonel Blaskic had visited the HVO commander in Busovaca and ordered the Muslim families or civilians in Busovaca to be ordered or, excuse me, to be protected by the local HVO?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: It was after my conversation with the mayor of Busovaca, and then I was told the following morning that Colonel Blaskic had visited Busovaca ordering the thing you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. And this was after again you had raised the point about Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And do you have any understanding as to why, any particular reason or motive, if you know, as to why Colonel Blaskic came to Busovaca and made this statement?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Things had changed a bit and maybe -- I express maybe he wanted to prevent an attack on Busovaca or he really realised that ethnic cleansing had to be stopped. I don't know. But the fact was that the families were protected.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. You said that maybe he wanted to prevent an attack on Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes. Could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, in your military experience, how would having the -- keeping these Muslims in Busovaca possibly prevent an attack on the town?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: You don't start shooting your own persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Directing you toward the latter part of June 1993. Did you come to know that the HVO, again being concerned of possible ABiH attacks around the Vitez pocket, and that Colonel Blaskic had created a unit which your Dutch battalion nicknamed or came to call the Fire Battalion?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what did you understand -- when you say Fire Battalion, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: A reserve battalion which would be used to operate in cases of emergency.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In some other military terms perhaps such a unit might be called a flying squad or a unit held in reserve to be manoeuvred very quickly to a point of attack?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you come to know that this Fire Battalion, as you called it, was located with headquarters at a particular location in the Busovaca-Vitez area?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: It was next to one of my transportation companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And where was that approximately?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: In the centre of Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you come to know who was the commanding officer of this Fire Battalion?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, Vlado Cosic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The same man that we saw in the photographs earlier?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that the soldiers that were used, at least in part, to form this unit had been previously part of a special, to your knowledge or assessment, a special HVO unit, dressed in black uniforms, who were used for special tasks by the HVO commanders -- I'll paraphrase a bit -- considered very tough or professional by your interpreter?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It was your understanding that these soldiers then formed this thing called the Fire Battalion?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did it come to your attention, sir, that Colonel Blaskic had some concerns about the ABiH possibly, again, attacking into Vitez and that he had moved his headquarters, at least temporarily, to an ammunition factory in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did it come to your attention that it was the position of the HVO leadership, Colonel Blaskic and Mr. Kordic, that they would never give up the pocket?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I object to the leading nature of this questioning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I'm sorry. I apologise, Your Honour. Mr. Kordic's name came into it. I was looking at Mr. Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me back up, Colonel. Did you come into any information at the time about any position of the HVO forces or side, as to their position in connection with this ammunition factory? Did some position they had stated or made known to you come to your attention --

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: They would never give up the ammunition factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And who did you -- to your knowledge, who were the individuals speaking for the Croat side on that particular occasion?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Mr. Kordic and Colonel Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In this same regard, did it come to your attention that essentially, if necessary, to prevent the factory from falling into the ABiH hands, the factory would be blown up and destroyed?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That was told, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did that cause you personally and your command concern?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: One of my other companies was located some kilometres away from the ammunition factory, and I feared toxic fumes to come free if they would execute that threat. So I got a message to Colonel Blaskic, asking him to give me a list of the raw materials which were in the factory. I got that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How did you receive it, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: By fax.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you take -- well, did you take this threat to blow up the factory seriously?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, in fact, you then turned around and faxed this same information that Colonel Blaskic had faxed to you and sent to your army staff here in The Hague; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What was your observation of the HVO command structure?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Efficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that on at least -- on one or more occasions when the DutchBat escorted, convoys were being held up at some location along the route, that you were able to intervene in the Vitez-Busovaca area and get the convoy freed up?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, they could.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court about a particular situation where you learned that one of your convoys was stopped at Metkovic, which again is on one of the locations that we looked at at the beginning of your testimony, on the maps, on the Exhibit 2612,13?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It may be, Your Honour, worth the point to just have that map on the ELMO or available to the Judges momentarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Looking at 2612,13, can you again point out to us Metkovic? And can you tell -- what did you learn -- what was reported to you about one of your convoys being stopped or held there?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Some of my convoys were sent to Mostar, and they were kept hostage by the Muslim factions, and as a reaction, my convoys were denied to leave Metkovic to come back to my location in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: It was not one convoy, there were at least five convoys. In those five convoys were soldiers who were due to return back to Holland. So I needed to get them back to Busovaca to start all the procedures to get them back in a proper way. We did not succeed in getting the convoys moving by our own means, either the battalions or UNPROFOR's. So I contacted Pasko Ljubicic and told him my problem, and I also told him it was pretty dumb, because the convoys were detailed to off-load their cargo in the Busovaca area. So if they did not return back there would be hunger in the Busovaca area. He promised to contact me later on, and a couple of hours later he told me that he had arranged the permission to move back to Busovaca. The next morning my convoys could roll on again and they returned back in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Part of this conversation, did Mr. Ljubicic say something to the effect that he would contact the commanding HVO officers or officials?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes. He told me the name of an HVO General in the southern part of Bosnia -- I do not remember the name -- he had spoken to, and this General had agreed to let the convoys go.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what happened the next morning?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: They could go.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And so looking at Exhibit 2612,13, this convoy had been stopped basically on the Croatian coast. And looking at the larger scale map which is 261,2 -- excuse me, 12,7, your intervention with Pasko Ljubicic in Busovaca was able to get that convoy free?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What was your observation or assessment of the HVO's communication capabilities?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Very modern, very high.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your observation and information sir, did the HVO appear to you to have portable telephones, fax machines, the public telephone network, and high-frequency radios?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: They had.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you've already mentioned one occasion. Is it fair to say that you personally received faxes from the HVO in the area on -- at least several times?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: One other situation where the convoy was -- a convoy was allowed -- arrangements were made for it to proceed, can you tell the Court about a convoy that was stopped at Lipa?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: There was a convoy stopped at the Lipa checkpoint, which was south of the mountains. It was stopped because the checkpoint crew wanted to check the cargo of my vehicles. My convoy commander refused that and the situation became pretty tense. It took the convoy commander about 45 minutes to an hour to get a message on by satellite to the battalion HQ telling what was going on. I again contacted Pasko Ljubicic, told him my problem, and asked him to interfere or to liase for me to the checkpoint. He promised me, and ten minutes later I got the message that the convoy is running again. That gave me the impression that I had underestimated the communications. They were very professional.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Looking -- excuse me. Looking at the map 2612,7, you may -- I don't know if you still have it there or not. My apologies to the usher. In any event, perhaps -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, we can proceed without it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This particular convoy, this area at the Lipa checkpoint, this was near Tomislavgrad?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This was some considerable distance in Western Bosnia or Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: But, again, within a matter of minutes, Mr. Ljubicic was able to get your convoy rolling?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you have occasions to travel with some of your convoys, Colonel?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the 13th of August, 1993, again in the Tomislavgrad area, did you see many cars and buses on the road between Tomislavgrad and Prozor?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And did you take any particular note or did anything come to mind at that occasion about what you were seeing?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: I had already heard quite a few rumours about the Croatian troops helping out the Bosnian troops. It makes you curious. I also had heard rumours about weekend rotations. As I was travelling on a Saturday and I got stuck in a lot of traffic along this route, and my curiosity was the main reason I took this photograph myself, because they show buses with soldiers, vans with soldiers, all going in a northern direction to Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The witness, Your Honour, is referring to -- has anticipated my next question, looking at Exhibit Z2780,1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is that a photograph, sir, that you took on the 13th of August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What were -- we can see what looks to be at least two buses on the left side of the road. What or who were in these buses?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There is a brown looking four-wheel drive type vehicle in the foreground of the photograph on the left side. Who was in that --

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Soldiers as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: During that time when you were stuck on this road, did you notice any licence plates on the vehicles being Croatian licence plates?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: I was just curious to find out what was going on there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: I couldn't trace the licence plates on the vehicles, so I intended to ask for their meaning later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you get any information later once you described these vehicles and described the licence plates as to --

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Not exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: But the licence plate, for instance, before we leave this photograph, on the rear of the red car, has the chequerboard emblem; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so the record is clear on that, I'm not -- the Court may or may not know, at this point, that licence plates in Bosnia-Herzegovina during this time period, also if there was a Croat area, if you will, a Croat region, they would often have or did have the chequerboard pattern as well. So I'm not suggesting that by itself means that it's a Croatian licence plate, and I just don't want the Court to think it's being misled.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: But you did not -- you were not able to come to any other particular information about this particular movement of troops that you saw in these vehicles moving north from Tomislavgrad to Prozor on the 13th of August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: We appreciated it to be normal duty, normal rotation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The rotation. The rotation of troops?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The final question or two, Colonel, in that area around Prozor, can you describe to the Court was there any particular feature or location in that area which was particularly military -- have particular military significance?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Makljen Ridge it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What was the military significance of that feature?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: It was the only checkpoint I ever saw in my six months where they had armoured vehicles stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you say "they," who is they?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: The HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And why, in your assessment, your military assessment, why would you have that particular checkpoint being especially heavily protected?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Because the Makljen Ridge was the key to the Prozor area and to the south part of Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And that is generally the area where you saw these troops being transported in mid-August of '93?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: The photograph that was taken south of Prozor and Makljen Ridge is north of Prozor, but the Prozor area was the area where most troops could disperse in several directions

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Court has heard about the attack that's in item 50, and I think we've covered that ground extensively. It's the attack about Grbavica near the BritBat camp. So we have no further questions, Your Honour. Thank you, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Sayers, it may be sensible to take the break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Does the Court want to take a break? That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: How long do you anticipate being?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I would think one hour and 15 minutes, perhaps. I'll try to do it in one hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And, Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Five, ten minutes maximum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll take a 20-minute break now, start again at 10 past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sayers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Good morning Colonel. My name is Steven Sayers. I represent the accused Dario Kordic. I have a few questions for you. I'll try to make them as brief as possible. A "yes" or a "no" answer would be appreciated, unless you feel that you need to elaborate, and just let me know if you do, and that would be fine. As I understand it, sir, you met Mr. Kordic on only two occasions during your seven months in Central Bosnia; first on May the 19th, 1993, and second on August the 16th, 1993?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: I believe I heard you say -- correct me if I'm wrong -- you never actually visited the Hotel Vitez yourself?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Nope.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Therefore, you never saw Mr. Kordic, obviously, at the Hotel Vitez in the company of Colonel Blaskic; did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Would you just take a look at one of the photographs which you were shown, Z2780,1. Yes, thank you. This photograph was taken in Bosnia-Herzegovina just northwest -- northeast of Metkovic, correct?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No, it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Where was it taken?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: It was taken on the road from Tomislavgrad up to Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Very well. Could I just ask you to concentrate on the two licence plates we can see in this photograph, Colonel. The first one says "RA" and then a symbol "122-AA"?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Let me put it to you, sir, that that is actually a licence plate from the town of Rama, also known as Prozor, in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: I never doubted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. And the second licence plate that you see, "CP," and it has, I think, a red star. That comes from the town of Caplijna, also in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you speak to any of the people in any of these vehicles?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you see any of their uniforms or things --

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: I just saw them all being in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You couldn't see the patches, could you?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: I wasn't interested in --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Fine. I understand. The photograph that you referred to containing the sniper's rifle, Z2780,3. The usher is just putting it on the ELMO. The gentleman in the flak jacket bending down, sir, do you recognise that as Colonel Darko Kraljevic, the Commander of the Vitezovi?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You don't recognise who it is?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Colonel, you have previously given a statement to the investigators who worked with the Prosecution, and that statement was given on January the 22nd and 23rd of 1997, correct?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that you have reviewed that statement carefully in preparation for coming to the Tribunal to testify today?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Your task was the transportation of humanitarian aid or assisting the transportation of humanitarian aid to dispersal centres on behalf of the UNHCR; I think that's what you have testified to today?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And you yourself, sir, do not speak any Croatian? Would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that actually during your seven-month tour in Central Bosnia you had little, if any, contact with Muslim military or political leaders?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: I had contact with military leaders.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You could not remember in your statement two years ago the name of the commanding officer of the 3rd Corps in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that you still do not remember that name?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: I still do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you actually meet him?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No. I met his intelligence officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: But your routine and daily contacts were almost entirely confined to Croat military personnel and -- well, actually, Croat military personnel, wouldn't that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No, because we always met the Muslim roadblock personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Were you aware that there was anyone viewed as the principal politician on the Muslim side in Central Bosnia when you were there, sir?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Do you know what the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna is or was?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: An institution by the name of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. We refer to it by its Croatian abbreviation, as an acronym, the HZ-HB. Have you ever heard of that?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Were you aware that on August the 28th, 1993, following the Owen-Stoltenberg Plan's signature by the Muslim side and the Croat side, an entity by the name of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna was formed?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You have no idea whether Mr. Kordic actually held any office within that republic, do you, sir?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Officially, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that you never met any of the other local Croat political figures from Vitez, such as Mr. Valenta, Anto Valenta?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: I know his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You've never met him, have you?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You never attended any at meetings at which he was present, have you, sir?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Mr. Ivica Santic. Does that name ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: The mayor of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you ever meet him?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Just to finish out this line of inquiry, three short questions. Have you ever met President Boban, the --

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Have you ever met Dr. Jadranko Prlic, who --

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. Did you know that he was the president of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: I heard about him but I never met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Have you ever met the head of the HVO defence department, Bruno Stojic?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Did you ever attend any of the weekly press conferences held by Mr. Kordic and others in either Busovaca or Vitez?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: The meeting, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Any press conferences?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: One press conference was held when I was due to leave for Holland again and I attended that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: All right. A few questions on the quality of life in Busovaca, sir.

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: You were there for seven months in a period of great turmoil would you not agree?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Unfortunately, the Vitez-Busovaca pocket was geographically isolated and surrounded by Muslim forces, correct?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: Life was pretty hard inside that pocket, I take it, sir.

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: It grew harder and harder.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
utterances.text: This Vitez-Busovaca pocket was geographically isolated from the other Croat pockets of Kiseljak, Zepce, Kakanj, and Vares; would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: PAULUS SCHIPPER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAYERS
